content:
Let total shares be normalized to 1, and sort shareholders’ shares as  
\[
a_1\le a_2\le \cdots \le a_{100}=x.
\]
Since any 66 shareholders own at least \(50\%\), the 66 smallest must satisfy
\[
a_1+\cdots+a_{66}\ge \frac12.
\]
Because \(a_{66}\) is the largest of these 66,
\[
a_{66}\ge \frac{1}{66}\cdot \frac12=\frac1{132}.
\]
Thus the 33 shareholders \(a_{67},\dots,a_{99}\) each have at least \(a_{66}\), so
\[
a_{67}+\cdots+a_{99}\ge 33\cdot \frac1{132}=\frac14.
\]
Therefore
\[
1=a_1+\cdots+a_{99}+x\ge \frac12+\frac14+x,
\]
so
\[
x\le \frac14.
\]
This is attainable by giving 99 shareholders \(1/132\) each and one shareholder \(1/4\).

\[
\boxed{25\%}
\]
